payload.recallText: I began my illustrious career as a journalist in the Bronx toiling as a hard-boiled writer at the Ram, the student newspaper at Fordham University. One day I was outside the library when I saw the elusive Dean McGowan, architect of a new policy to replace Fordham's working-to-middle-class with more prestigious students. I approached him and said "Dean McGowan, is it true Fordham plans to raise tution significantly above inflation rate and, if so, doesn't that go against it's mission?". Dean McGowan stepped toward me and said "Listen here, punk". In the corner of my eye, a blur turned into a man with a cream pie which turned into the cream pie being thrown at Dean McGowan's face. "Care to comment?" I asked. "Yeah I care to comment. Fuck you," said Dean McGowan. I rushed back to tell Billy Dwyer, the editor of the Ram, and he'd go on to win a Pulitzer, which is true, and he's a big guy. "Dean McGowan? That guy's a dick. Write it up". I sat down banging away at my story, and I knew it was good, when I started to add some extra detail called embellishment. Journalists advise against this practice and consider it crossing the line, but I had already seen the line crossed between an evil dean and an assault with a cream pie. First I gave him a name "Pie Man", capital P, capital M. Then I said he was wearing a cape and a mask, but he was capeless. Finally I gave him a catchphrase. It means "I am not an animal" which doesn't make any sense. I'm Catholic, Latin just comes to me.
